record.original_question: Either construct an irreducible geodesic net in the Euclidean plane with four unbalanced vertices and more than 16 balanced vertices, or prove that no such geodesic net exists. Here irreducible means that no proper subset of its edges, together with the incident vertices, is itself a geodesic net with the same set of unbalanced vertices.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2.1. Find an irreducible geodesic net with 4 unbalanced vertices in the Euclidean plane with more than 16 balanced vertices (or prove that such a geodesic net does not exist.)

one can define irreducible geodesic nets on a given set S of unbalanced vertices as geodesic nets such that no subgraph formed by a proper subset of the set of edges (with all incident vertices) is a geodesic net with the same set S of unbalanced vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A geodesic net is a finite straight-line embedded graph $G=(V,E)$ together with a partition $V = V_u \sqcup V_b$ into unbalanced vertices and balanced vertices, such that at every balanced vertex $v \in V_b$ the sum of the unit tangent vectors along the edges incident to $v$ equals zero (the balancing condition). Edges are straight segments and are required to meet only at vertices. A geodesic net with set of unbalanced vertices $S = V_u$ is called irreducible if no proper subset $E' \subsetneq E$ of its edges, taken together with all vertices incident to $E'$, forms a geodesic net having the same set $S$ of unbalanced vertices.

Either exhibit an irreducible geodesic net in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose set of unbalanced vertices has cardinality $4$ and which has strictly more than $16$ balanced vertices, or prove that no such geodesic net exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A construction published in November 2025 exhibits an irreducible geodesic net in the Euclidean plane with 4 unbalanced (boundary) vertices and 25 balanced vertices, increasing the previously known maximum from 16 to 25, thereby answering the existence side of the problem affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: a geodesic net in the plane with four boundary (unbalanced) vertices that has 25 balanced vertices and that is irreducible ... increases the previously known maximum for balanced vertices of nets of this kind from 16 to 25.
status_evidence.claim: An irreducible geodesic net in the plane with 4 unbalanced vertices and 25 (>16) balanced vertices has been constructed.
